Grace — quick technical notes (I pulled these from the presign service and KMS audit):

- Presign flow: request -> presign-service (runs in Redbox VPC) -> signs request using a KMS-delegated asymmetric key alias redwood/brightpeak/presign (we use KMS GenerateDataKey/Sign depending on scheme). The presign signing key is never exported. I'll attach a simple diagram.
- TTL: default 15 minutes for object uploads; some legacy customers had 1h but BrightPeak's profile is set to 15m. No long-lived prefixes.
- KMS rotation: keys use an alias pattern redwood/brightpeak/presign/v{N}. Rotation events exported via CloudAudit — I've pulled 12 months into kms_rotation_event_log.csv (redacted principal ARNs).
- Access controls: only the presign-service role (arn:aws:iam::REDACTED:role/presign-service) and our deployment pipeline role can call kms:Sign/GenerateDataKey/* on the presign alias. I'll include a sanitized IAM snippet showing the allowed principal ARNs and the condition limiting calls to the presign API.

I'll attach: archer_presign_kms_diagram.png and kms_rotation_event_log.csv (redacted). Markus — if you can prepare the attestation wording (short, confirms TTL, rotation cadence, private key non-export), I can inline the technical bits.

Jonas
